milestones.title: Records cleanup
milestones.description: The evaluation records and the measurement programme's code are removed, and code comments that cite removed decisions are rewritten.

milestones.title: Release
milestones.description: Focrux is developed in lianmatsuo/focrux, which carries everything that runs on one machine, with every corpus fixture published in plantedbugs (D-075, D-076); the first release carries a signed tag, a SHA-256 and a provenance attestation (D-046).

milestones.title: First people
milestones.description: The co-founder uses Focrux, and the design partner starts once D-084's list holds.

milestones.title: The loop
milestones.description: The loop's decided, unbuilt capabilities and its open defects.

issues.title: Onboard the first design partner
issues.outcome: The first design partner runs their own work through Focrux, with their direct-agent baseline captured before their first ticket (D-084, D-038).
acceptance_criteria: The rename has landed and the partner has an installable build.
The partner's direct-agent baseline is captured with `focrux baseline` before their first ticket.
The partner has the disclosure and has signed the one-page agreement, which a lawyer has read (D-047).

issues.title: A decline that reports a closure is not a decline: harden the channel's semantics
issues.outcome: The NO_PRACTICE channel carries only what it means: no determinable practice, and a person decides. A decline whose finding the change in fact closed is caught rather than escalated as a question for a person (D-065).
acceptance_criteria: The register records how a closure declared through NO_PRACTICE is caught: by the brief's wording, by verification treating a closed declined finding as closed with a note, or by a distinct section of the pull request body.
A test drives an executor that fixes a routed finding and then declares NO_PRACTICE about it, and the loop does not present it to a person as undecided.

issues.title: `doctor` and `run` report an executor that is not signed in
issues.outcome: A missing executor login is a sentence from `focrux doctor` and from the preflight of `focrux run`, as a missing binary already is.
acceptance_criteria: `focrux doctor` reports an executor CLI that is present but not signed in, naming the command that signs it in.
`focrux run` refuses to start on that finding and leaves the ticket in its prior state.

issues.title: The reviewer's `claude` transport and the delivery test are pinned to what they do
issues.outcome: The reviewer's `claude` transport closes every repository-supplied configuration the executor's adapter closes, and its test names the reviewer's own list; the delivery test exercises the delivery code rather than matching its source text.
acceptance_criteria: One test pins the configuration each `claude` transport closes, and the reviewer's closes at least what the executor's adapter does.
`delivery-idempotent.test.ts` drives the delivery code against a fake `gh` instead of reading `delivery.ts` as text.

issues.title: Closure verification short-circuits on a truncated change set
issues.outcome: A remediation round whose sealed change set was too large to review fails closed without a model call.
acceptance_criteria: `verifyClosures` returns every routed finding as `cannot_tell`, with a deterministic failure naming the byte size, when the change set is truncated, before the checks or the model are consulted.
That verification records `cost_basis: not_incurred` and zero usage.
A test drives `verifyClosures` with a truncated change set and a model stub that throws if it is called.

issues.title: Every finding names a file and a line, or says it cannot
issues.outcome: Every finding names a file and a line, or says why it cannot: the review schema requires a location or an explicit `unlocatable` with a reason, and the reviewer's prompt asks for one.
acceptance_criteria: A finding with neither a file nor `unlocatable` is rejected by the artifact schema, and the prompt-version test pins the instruction.
The corpus harness reports the share of findings that could not be located on each run.
The change carries a regression-suite run (D-010).

issues.title: A loop merge trusts only a D-073 verdict the review run itself left: the comment's author is checked, not only its shape
issues.outcome: The loop's merge accepts a D-073 verdict only from the identity the repository names for review runs, so no other account can write the comment that lets the loop merge (D-041, D-073).
acceptance_criteria: A verdict comment from any other author is refused as `merge.no_separate_approval`, naming the author, and the same comment from the configured author is accepted.
A configuration without `review.verdict_author` never merges under `merge: loop`, and says why.
The loop's own review run records the author it posts as, and `focrux doctor --write-config` proposes the key.

issues.title: Admission names a scope that reaches what judges an attempt when the contract is drafted
issues.outcome: A scope that reaches what judges an attempt is named when the contract is drafted or typed, so a person sees it before editing the scope rather than at approval (D-079).
acceptance_criteria: `focrux admit` reports a scope that overlaps a pinned check's definition, a protected path or `.focrux/**`, naming both, before the person edits it.
`focrux approve` still refuses such a contract with the same statement.

issues.title: A contract cannot both allow and prohibit a path
issues.outcome: A contract cannot both allow and prohibit a path: editing the allowed paths to reach inside a prohibited glob drops that prohibition and says so, and approval refuses a contract that still does.
acceptance_criteria: `focrux edit --path` on a `plan_review` ticket, adding a path inside one of its prohibited globs, removes that prohibition and prints the removal.
`focrux approve` refuses a contract whose allowed path lies inside one of its prohibited globs, naming both.

issues.title: A finding's blocking reason carries no decision identifier
issues.outcome: Every blocking reason the router writes says why in plain words, with no decision or backlog id in it.
acceptance_criteria: A test walks every reason `decideBlocking` and `routeForReview` can produce, under every policy, and fails on a `D-0nn` or `SCP-nnn` in any of them.
`repolicy.ts` still reads a demotion back out of the reason string.
No routing outcome changes under any policy.

issues.title: A re-run of a ticket whose last review was incomplete resumes as a re-review, not as a verification round
issues.outcome: A re-run of a ticket whose last review was `incomplete` re-reviews the round, as the first pass does, rather than verifying findings that were never closed.
acceptance_criteria: A ticket whose last review bundle is `incomplete`, run again, reaches the reviewer after the round, not the closure verifier.
A ticket whose last review is a complete verdict resumes as before.

issues.title: A test added to close an evidence finding fails without the change, and the closure verifier reads that it does
issues.outcome: A test written to close an evidence finding discriminates: the brief asks for a test that fails without the change, and the closure verifier does not accept one that would pass on the unchanged tree.
acceptance_criteria: A round that closes an `evidence.*` finding with a test asserting only behaviour the base already had is verified `not_closed`, naming the test.
A round whose test depends on the change's new behaviour is verified closed.
The remediation brief for an evidence finding states the requirement in one sentence.

issues.title: A remediation round closes its findings and nothing else
issues.outcome: A remediation round makes the smallest change that closes its findings, and a round that spends the expansion budget says so in the pull request.
acceptance_criteria: The remediation brief asks for the smallest change that closes the routed findings and names what it must not add.
A round that touches files outside the admitted paths within the expansion budget records them on the attempt as `expansion_used`, and the pull request body names them.
The scope assessment, the widening refusal and the routing do not change.

issues.title: The loop's merge gate reads a check run still in progress as pending, and its stop says so
issues.outcome: The loop's merge step reads a check run that has not concluded as still running, names it so in the stop, and still refuses to merge on it.
acceptance_criteria: A rollup entry with `status: IN_PROGRESS` and an empty conclusion reaches the merge decision as unconcluded, and `merge.checks_not_green` names it as in progress.
A rollup whose entries have all concluded reads as before.

issues.title: Commit signing is the person's choice: the loop's merge gate reads the repository's rule, not its own
issues.outcome: The loop's merge never refuses an unsigned commit on its own account: it requires a verified signature only where the base branch's protection does, and then names that rule as the repository's (D-091).
acceptance_criteria: Given unsigned commits and a base branch that does not require signatures, the merge decision reaches the mergeable path; given one that does, it stops with `merge.unverified_signature`, naming the repository's protection.
The merge step reads the base branch's signature rule once, beside its other reads, and records it on the merge outcome.

issues.title: A run whose checkout's history is not the base branch's publishes a readable pull request, or refuses before it executes
issues.outcome: A run whose checkout does not share recent history with `base_ref` either merges the base in before the executor starts, so the pull request shows the change alone, or refuses before any attempt with the line that fixes it.
acceptance_criteria: A checkout that shares only an old merge-base with `base_ref` publishes a pull request whose diff against the base is the attempt's change alone.
A checkout whose base cannot be merged cleanly is refused before the executor, with the conflict named.
`focrux doctor` says when the checkout's HEAD is not on the base branch's history, and `focrux inspect` shows the merge-base the attempt was cut from.

issues.title: A merged local run is observable: its escape window and its stop answers are filed like a ticket's
issues.outcome: A merged local run is observed like a ticket: `focrux sync` files its escape window and stop answers, `focrux escapes` reads the window, and `focrux stops` counts the answers.
acceptance_criteria: The escape and stop-verdict records accept a local run's id where there is no ticket key, and records with a ticket key read as before.
After `focrux sync` over a store holding a merged local run, `focrux escapes` prints its window and `focrux stops` reads its answers.
`apps/cli/README.md` describes both records as written for local runs.

issues.title: The loop's merge waits for GitHub to compute mergeability before it reads it
issues.outcome: The loop's merge waits a bounded time for GitHub to compute mergeability, and stops only on `conflicting` or on an `unknown` that outlasts the bound.
acceptance_criteria: A `gh` fake answering `unknown` twice and then `mergeable` merges; one answering `unknown` past the bound stops, naming the bound; one answering `conflicting` stops at once.
The stop says whether GitHub had not yet computed mergeability or had found a conflict.

issues.title: A stop's answerer is read from GitHub's own record of who ticked, not only from the body's `by=` field
issues.outcome: A stop's answerer rests on who GitHub records as having edited the pull request body, not only on the `by=` field; where the two disagree, the stop is set aside from partner readings and counted.
acceptance_criteria: A box ticked with a `by=` naming a bot by an account GitHub records as a person, and one ticked without `by=` by an App, are recorded as disagreements, left out of partner readings, and counted by `focrux stops`.
`focrux sync` reads the body's edit history through `gh`, and the record names which source the answerer rests on.

issues.title: A transport's last line is read and recorded whether or not its newline arrived, and the fake transport drains before it exits
issues.outcome: An attempt's record carries every line its transport wrote, including a final line with no newline: the adapter flushes the partial line it holds when the stream ends, and the test fake drains its output before it exits.
acceptance_criteria: A fake stream whose final `tool_use` line has no trailing newline is counted, judged and recorded.
A fake that writes five thousand lines and exits is read whole by a deliberately slow reader.
The fake transport in `packages/runner/test/support.ts` sets `process.exitCode` and returns rather than calling `process.exit`.

issues.title: Carry an execution graph in the plan, drafted from a spec
issues.outcome: A plan can group its acceptance criteria into nodes, each with the paths expected to satisfy them, and the Ticket's approach holds the suggested order between nodes and the spec's No-Gos; the drafter turns a spec into one contract with a suggested graph, one edit path changes an unapproved graph, and inspect shows the graph and its size estimate.
acceptance_criteria: The plan schema accepts nodes whose criteria and paths are part of the contract, refuses a criterion outside every node and a node path outside the allowed scope, and still accepts a plan without nodes.
A criterion may record the requirement id it was drafted from; the schema refuses an id the spec does not carry, and a plan drafted from an issue carries none.
The approach record holds edges and No-Gos, may change after approval, and is not part of what the reviewer receives.
The drafter, under a new prompt version, returns one contract with nodes and suggested edges, has no upper limit on criteria, and refuses a cycle.
No-Gos are read from the spec's No-Gos heading, not drafted by the model.
inspect and --json show nodes, edges and a size estimate from S to XL derived by fixed thresholds from nodes, criteria, and files and packages in scope.

focrux edit applies graph edits — add, split, merge and delete nodes; change a criterion or a node's paths; add or remove an edge — to an unapproved plan, validating each, recording its author, and undoing any edit on request under D-100's rule, naming the later edit that blocks one.
docs/04 documents the node and approach fields, and the root README no longer promises two to four criteria.
issues.notes: Decided in D-100, D-103 and D-104; extends ADR-0016.

issues.title: Make the documents agree about the gate and about what CI runs
issues.outcome: AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/07, ADR-0007 and docs/evaluation/regression-suite.md describe one gate and one truth about GitHub Actions, and a contributor can produce the regression summary a reviewing run asks for.
acceptance_criteria: One list of what the gate runs, in one file, cited by the others; today AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and build.yml each name a different set, and the protected-paths check appears in none of them.
No document asserts that a workflow runs while Actions are off; each says what a person runs instead.
The regression section names where the corpus comes from, so its commands can be followed without guessing --corpus, which silently scores against the working tree.
The section says the unstated_regression row comes from <out>/report.md's recall-by-class table, not from the delta table, which carries metrics only.
A contributor following the section end to end produces the summary AGENTS.md requires in a pull-request body, proven by one dry run.
issues.notes: Found by the D-073 reviews of #678, which split this out. The contradictions predate that change.

issues.title: Put Create first in the rail and open planning mode
issues.outcome: Create sits first in the rail and opens planning mode for one piece of work in a chosen repository, with the current drafting steps in its Spec pane; the header button goes and Home's empty state keeps its own.
acceptance_criteria: The rail reads Create, Home, Archive, Settings; ⌘1 to ⌘4 follow that order, ⌘N still creates, and rebinding still refuses a conflict.
Create opens a small repository picker with any open drafts listed first, and Enter resumes the top one.
Planning mode shows its child icons under Create only while planning; leaving returns to Home, and the draft survives a restart as a contract editing session.
Home's header has no Create button; its empty state still offers one.
The phone boards are unchanged.
The flow tests drive Create from the rail.

issues.title: Plan while a run is going
issues.outcome: Drafting, impact checks, file reads and the interview run alongside a loop run, while runs, decisions and publishing still take one at a time.
acceptance_criteria: Starting a draft while a run is active succeeds; starting a second run still answers that another command is active.
Two drafts in flight for different sessions each land on their own session.
docs/15 says what runs alongside a run.

issues.title: Keep specs as folders and draft the first plan from them
issues.outcome: Planning mode keeps a spec at specs/<slug>/spec.md under fixed headings, creating the folders when missing; Generate plan drafts the first plan from it and admits one Ticket in plan_review; admission records the spec's path and content hash; specs/** joins the standing prohibited paths; and the folder carries a generated page for each node.
acceptance_criteria: The first spec in a repository creates specs/; the slug comes from the spec's title, deterministically.
The spec has the headings Outcome, Requirements, No-Gos, Rabbit holes and Notes, and the drafter receives it as delimited data, as it receives an issue.
A requirement written in the spec is given an id, R1 upward, never reused; editing its text keeps its id, and a re-draft keeps the ids.
A requirement's node is derived from the criteria drafted from it and shown beside it in the Spec pane: one whose criteria sit in several nodes shows each, and one with no criterion yet shows none.

specs/<slug>/nodes/<node>.md is generated from the spec and the graph, carries the node's title, the requirements derived to it, its criteria and their verification, its paths and the spec's No-Gos, and is regenerated when either changes.
A hand-written Notes section in a node's page survives regeneration, and the test fails first.
After the first draft the plan changes only by edits; Start over from the spec re-drafts the same Ticket after confirmation and never admits another, and the test fails first.
Admission records the spec's path and content hash.
An executor write under specs/ is refused as a prohibited path.
Start over from the spec drops the graph edits and the paths they added, and keeps spec edits, explorer marks and No-Gos.
Supporting files may sit beside spec.md; only spec.md is drafted from.

issues.title: Show the drafter the repository's CONTEXT.md, ADR titles and principles
issues.outcome: The drafter also receives the repository's CONTEXT.md, its ADR titles and principles.md as repository data, each recorded on the draft snapshot like a file read.
acceptance_criteria: Where they exist, all three appear in the drafter's context as delimited repository data; where none exists, the call is unchanged.
Each counts against the drafter's read limits and is recorded on the draft snapshot.
The draft prompt version changes.

issues.title: Run the interview on Claude: focrux interview
issues.outcome: focrux interview runs a person's own Claude Code session through the Claude Agent SDK, oriented with the bundled grilling and domain-modelling skills and streaming JSON; it reads anything, runs read-only commands, writes only the spec's folder, CONTEXT.md and the ADR folder, and refuses anything else.
acceptance_criteria: A write outside the spec's folder, CONTEXT.md or the ADR folder is refused by the executor's guard; the test fails first.
A generate request makes the session bring spec.md up to date with the conversation, and report that it has, before any drafting starts.

After the first draft, the session changes the plan only through the interview's edit tool, each change validated and recorded with the interview as its author, and updates the spec to match; a direct write to the ticket store is refused.
A command outside the read-only set is refused and reported as refused, never put to the person, and the test fails first.
The session has no way to approve, publish or merge.
Resuming with the same session continues the conversation.
Missing spec and ADR folders are created on first write.
Nothing is copied from Paseo, whose current code is AGPL-3.0; its design is followed.
issues.notes: Decided in D-102. Adds the Claude Agent SDK as a pinned catalog dependency.

issues.title: Run the interview on Codex
issues.outcome: The same interview runs through codex app-server behind the same session interface, with the same write rules, refusals and resume.
acceptance_criteria: The interview's contract tests pass against both transports.
Command and file-change requests follow the interview's rules; anything else is refused, and the transport's own approval question never reaches the person.
Resume uses the thread's own resume.

issues.title: Keep the interview chat docked in planning mode, editing the plan in place
issues.outcome: The interview chat stays docked beside every planning pane from the first question to approval — messages, tool calls as cards, and a refusal where the session may not act. Generate plan makes the first draft; after that, what the person asks for is applied to the plan and the spec as edits, each shown as a before-and-after card with Undo. The provider and model default to the drafting choice, and the conversation is kept with the draft.
acceptance_criteria: The chat stays visible and usable while the Spec, Explorer, Graph or Impact pane is open.
The host relays focrux interview's events to the renderer and answers back on the same session; renderer requests still carry repository ids, not paths.
The session never asks for permission: a command it may not run and a write it may not make are each refused and shown as refused, in a test.
The plan's history opens as a drawer over the current pane, so the chat stays visible, and each entry is labelled you or interview.
Leaving planning mode, and restarting the app, restore the conversation.
An edit from the chat changes only what it names, hand edits elsewhere survive, and Undo restores the plan as it stood before that edit, under D-100's rule.

issues.title: Commit the spec first and review the diff after it
issues.outcome: The loop commits the spec folder, with the CONTEXT.md and ADR changes recorded at admission, as the first commit on the Ticket's branch, and review reads the diff from after that commit.
acceptance_criteria: The branch's first commit holds exactly the recorded spec files, and a hash mismatch stops the run before execution.
The reviewed diff excludes that commit; the reviewer may still open the spec as it opens any file.
Re-levels and remediation rounds keep the review base at the spec commit.

issues.title: Mark a spec stale when it or the code it names changes
issues.outcome: A spec edited after approval, or naming an @Symbol or path that no longer exists, is stale: an unstarted Ticket goes to plan_invalid and needs approving again, and a running one is flagged and carries on.
acceptance_criteria: Editing the spec after approval moves an unstarted Ticket to plan_invalid, in a test over a real store.
Removing an exported symbol the spec names marks the spec stale.
A running Ticket shows the flag and its run is not interrupted.
docs/04's lifecycle section and its diagram agree on any transition this adds.

issues.title: Curate and approve the graph in the Graph pane
issues.outcome: The Graph pane shows the drafted graph and its size estimate; the person adds, splits, merges and deletes nodes, edits each node's criteria and paths, draws and removes edges, and approves once, also for any Ticket in plan_review.
acceptance_criteria: Every edit changes the canonical contract or approach fields and counts in the admission edit log.
Approving from the Graph pane produces the contract the runner reads, on the fixed approve binding.
Edits from the Graph pane and from the chat share one edit path and one history, each recorded with its author and undoable; Start over from the spec replaces the plan only after confirmation.
The size estimate updates as the graph changes.
The graph view pans: dragging the empty canvas or scrolling moves it, so a large graph works with the node panel open.
Selecting a node shows its generated page, read-only, beside its criteria and paths.
The graph library works under the desktop's content-security policy, which allows no workers.
issues.notes: Decided in D-100, D-101, D-103 and D-104.

issues.title: Keep the graph live during a run
issues.outcome: While a Ticket runs, its graph shows per node which paths have changed and each criterion's state from checks and review, derived only from records.
acceptance_criteria: A node's state comes from the sealed change set and review coverage; an executor transcript claiming completion changes nothing, in a test.
Changed paths outside every node are shown as outside.

issues.title: Browse, preview and mark paths in the explorer
issues.outcome: The explorer lists the repository's tracked files and previews one read-only; the person marks paths allowed or prohibited in the draft's scope, or prohibits a path in the repository's standing list.
acceptance_criteria: New host requests take a repository id and a repository-relative path, pass safePath and the reviewer's never-read list, and refuse anything else.

Marks change the draft's canonical scope; the always option is a checkbox with no confirmation, writes the standing list in .focrux/config.json, is recorded in the draft's history and can be undone, and the standing list shows which draft added it.
The preview is read-only and size-capped.
The host's stated rule about renderer requests is amended where it is written.

issues.title: Index TypeScript and JavaScript symbols and imports
issues.outcome: focrux index builds, on demand, the exported symbols and import graph of a TS/JS repository with TypeScript's parser, for impact warnings, @Symbol completion and stale-spec checks.
acceptance_criteria: The exported declarations and import edges of a fixture monorepo match a hand-written expectation; the test fails first.
A repository outside TypeScript and JavaScript gets an explicit unsupported answer, not an empty index.
The bundled CLI's size change is recorded.
issues.notes: Decided in D-015. Makes typescript a runtime dependency of the CLI bundle (D-046).

issues.title: Show impact warnings in planning mode
issues.outcome: On demand, planning mode lists impact warnings — files and packages outside the draft's scope that import what it changes or what the spec names, plus the path classes risk.ts recognises — and the person can turn a warning into a scope change or a No-Go.
acceptance_criteria: Warnings are advice and never become action parameters without the person's edit.
Turning a warning into a scope change edits the draft's scope; into a No-Go, it appends to the spec's No-Gos.
A repository outside TypeScript and JavaScript shows only the path-class warnings, and says so.

issues.title: Edit the spec with @Symbol completion
issues.outcome: The Spec pane edits the spec directly, completing @Symbol from the index and marking names the index cannot find.
acceptance_criteria: Typing @ offers exported symbols, and choosing one inserts it.
An unknown @Name is marked in the editor.
The person's edits and the interview's writes to the same file never silently overwrite each other.

issues.title: Refuse writes to prohibited paths before they happen
issues.outcome: The write guard refuses a write to a prohibited path inside the allowed ones, with the same paths_prohibited match the reviewer uses, and the reviewer's blocking finding stays as the backstop.
acceptance_criteria: A prohibited-inside-allowed write is refused before it happens on both transports; the test fails first.
The paths.ts comment states the new rule and its reason.
The reviewer's scope.prohibited_path finding is unchanged.

issues.title: Run without cost, token or wall-clock ceilings, and stop a stalled attempt
issues.outcome: An attempt has no cost, token or wall-clock ceiling; a stall detector stops one with no tool activity for a set time; the remediation-round limit stays; a cost cap applies only when the executor is billed per token; usage is shown as providers report it.
acceptance_criteria: A long attempt with steady tool activity is never stopped, with a fake transport.
An attempt with no tool activity for the configured time stops as stalled, a termination reason documented in docs/04.
With an API key in the executor's environment, the cost cap still applies.
limits.ts, the desktop's ceilings dialog and General's ceiling-stop notification follow the change.

issues.title: Give the brief back after every compaction
issues.outcome: After every compaction the executor, and each subagent, receives its brief again: outcome, criteria by node, scope and prohibited paths, No-Gos, principles.md, each node's state from the records, and open findings.
acceptance_criteria: On Claude, a SessionStart hook matching compact in the runner's settings file re-injects the brief.
On Codex, the main thread's SessionStart compact hook re-injects it; a sub-agent thread gets it through thread/inject_items after its contextCompaction item.
The re-injected brief is the attempt's recorded brief plus the current state block.

issues.title: Test subagents live on both transports
issues.outcome: A recorded live test answers, on Claude Code 2.1.247 and Codex 0.145.0, whether the runner's guard sees each subagent's tool calls and which agent made them, how subagent events and usage are reported, whether reported cost includes subagents, whether Codex children keep the read-only sandbox and untrusted approvals, and whether children load instruction sources.
acceptance_criteria: Each question is answered with a transcript excerpt, or recorded as undecided with the reason.
The answers are recorded in ADR-0038 before SCP-326 starts.
issues.notes: Decided in D-106. Decides whether SCP-326 and SCP-327 are built as drafted.

issues.title: Let the Claude executor start subagents
issues.outcome: The Claude executor may start subagents from Focrux-defined roles; every subagent write passes the Ticket's scope guard, repository and personal agent definitions stay unreachable, every subagent's activity is recorded against it, and review receives none of it.
acceptance_criteria: The executor may start only Focrux's roles; a definition in ~/.claude/agents cannot be started, in a test.
The guard keeps its state per agent and loses nothing under interleaved calls; the test fails first.
Command records name the agent, and only the top-level session's final message becomes the executor's account.

issues.title: Let the Codex executor start subagents
issues.outcome: The Codex executor may use Codex's multi-agent feature with Focrux-defined roles in place of the built-ins, handling approvals, items and usage per thread, on Codex 0.145.0 or later.
acceptance_criteria: A child's approvals are judged by the same guard with its own working directory, and usage is summed per thread rather than overwritten; the tests fail first.
Focrux's role definitions replace the built-in roles in the runner's isolated CODEX_HOME.
doctor refuses a Codex older than 0.145.0 and names the version.
Sub-agent threads receive the brief after compaction.

issues.title: Review a graph per node and once overall
issues.outcome: A Ticket with an execution graph is reviewed once per node, on that node's criteria and the part of the diff inside its paths, and once over the whole change for the outcome, anything that crosses nodes, and any path allowed in the explorer that no node names, with the gate combining them.
acceptance_criteria: The pull request carries a regression-suite run with the unstated_regression row first.
New graph-shaped fixtures exercise per-node review, including a planted defect that crosses nodes.
A node's review receives that node's check results, and a node whose checks failed is reviewed with them.
The overall review covers a path allowed in the explorer that no node names, in a test.
A Ticket without a graph is reviewed exactly as before.
issues.notes: Decided in D-107. A change to the reviewer, so it carries a regression-suite run (D-010).

issues.title: Run the pinned checks per node
issues.outcome: A Ticket with an execution graph runs its pinned checks once per node, narrowed to that node's paths, and records each node's results with the attempt.
acceptance_criteria: Each node's result names the check, the paths it was narrowed to and its status, and the test fails first.
A check that cannot be narrowed runs once over the change and is recorded as such.
A node whose checks fail does not stop the other nodes' checks, and the whole-change checks still run.
A Ticket without a graph runs its checks exactly as before.
issues.notes: Decided in D-107. Narrowing reuses the rerun's file scope in packages/contracts/src/check.ts.

issues.title: Check No-Gos in review
issues.outcome: The contract carries No-Gos, the executor is briefed with them, and the reviewer checks that the change implements none of them.
acceptance_criteria: The pull request carries a regression-suite run and adds fixtures that violate a No-Go.
The blocking severity of a No-Go finding is decided before the prompt changes.
issues.notes: Deferred by D-107: until it lands, No-Gos brief the executor and nothing checks them.

issues.title: Critique a draft adversarially before approval
issues.outcome: An advisory critic examines a drafted contract and graph for missed edge cases, concurrency and security gaps before approval, measured before it ships.
acceptance_criteria: Its questions reach the person as advice and never change the contract on their own.
It is measured on real drafts before it is enabled.
issues.notes: Deferred: the interview critiques a draft when asked.

issues.title: The provisioning verify runs uncached, so the base's answer is the base's and not a replay
issues.outcome: The materialisation's verify command runs against the worktree as it stands and never replays a task cache produced elsewhere: a verify that a task runner would serve from its cache runs with the cache bypassed, and the record says whether its answer came from a run or a replay, so the base verification and the pinned checks cannot disagree about the same tree.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest whose verify is a turbo invocation without `--force` runs with the cache bypassed, or is refused with the reason, and the recorded verification names the run as uncached.
A verify whose output reports a cache hit for any task is not recorded as a pass.
`focrux doctor` proposes a verify command that bypasses the task cache where the repository's task runner has one.

issues.title: `doctor` answers "materializable" the way an attempt would: a scratch worktree installed with scripts off and the checks run uncached
issues.outcome: `focrux doctor` provisions a scratch worktree the way an attempt does (the manifest's install with its lifecycle-scripts policy, no developer node_modules, no task cache) and runs the pinned checks there uncached, so "materializable" means an attempt can build and check the repository, and a package that needs a script-installed binary is named before any attempt runs.
acceptance_criteria: A repository whose build needs a binary that a lifecycle script installs reports `materializable: false`, naming the package and the policy that keeps it out; a repository that builds under the attempt's install reports true.
The report names what it measured in (the scratch worktree, the install command, the bypassed cache), and `--write-config` proposes the exception or check filter a person can choose.
The scratch worktree is removed after the diagnosis, and the diagnosis makes no model call.

issues.title: A merged pull request settles its ticket: `merged` from any state that carries it, and the loop's own merge walks it there
issues.outcome: A ticket whose pull request `gh` reports merged reads `merged`, whatever state it was in when the merge happened, and `sync --merge` walks the ticket to `merged` in the command that merged it, with the stop that escalated it recorded as answered by the merge. `inspect` and `sync` never show a merged pull request beside a ticket that still waits on someone.
acceptance_criteria: A ticket in `changes_requested` whose recorded pull request `gh` reports merged is walked to `merged` by `sync`.
`sync --merge` that merges the pull request leaves the ticket `merged` before it returns, and the escalation's stop reads answered by the merge, with the approving verdict's head.
A merged pull request on a ticket in any non-terminal state is the same transition, named in the ticket's history as reconciled from `gh`.

issues.title: The scope-widening refusal reads the deterministic path-scope findings only, never a model-minted rule id that starts with `scope.`
issues.outcome: A remediation round is refused for widening only when it was given one of the harness's own path-scope findings (`scope.escape`, `scope.prohibited_path`, `scope.expansion_budget_exceeded`, `scope.generated_without_source`) and added paths the previous round's change set did not hold. A semantic finding filed under a `scope.` rule id is routed and verified like any other semantic finding, and a round that closes it by adding files inside the contract's globs is verified, not refused.
acceptance_criteria: A remediation round given only a model-minted `scope.*` finding that adds a file inside `paths_allowed` is verified, not refused.
A round given `scope.escape` that adds a path outside the previous round's change set is still refused, with the same stop text.
The rule ids the refusal reads are one exported list in `packages/contracts/src` that the loop reads, so a new deterministic scope rule joins it in one edit.

issues.title: A conflict round resolves a merge in progress and is sealed as a merge commit, so the base is in the branch's history when the round ends
issues.outcome: When the base will not merge into the attempt branch, the runner leaves the conflicted merge in the worktree rather than aborting it, the conflict round resolves the markers in place, and the seal completes the merge with the base tip as the commit's second parent, so the merge-up that follows is a no-op. A round that leaves a marker still ends `base_conflict`, naming the file.
acceptance_criteria: A branch and a base that both change one region of a file, with an executor that resolves the markers in place, end with the base tip as an ancestor of the branch and the run continuing to its review.
The seal of a conflict round is a merge commit whose parents are the previous sealed head and the base tip, carries the attempt trailer, and is read by `describeRange` as the branch against the base.
A conflict round that leaves a marker, or runs the executor to a ceiling, still ends `base_conflict` with the same stop text, with the merge aborted so nothing half-merged is sealed.

issues.title: The guard's working directory does not move on a command the hook refused, and a target it cannot place after a lost `cd` refuses one command rather than ending the attempt
issues.outcome: The guard's model of the shell's working directory advances only on commands that ran: a `cd` inside a command the pre-tool hook refused never happened, so the model stays where it was. Where the model has lost the directory (a `cd` to a target it could not read, in a command that ran), a later relative target is refused as that one command, with a reason that says to use a path from the worktree root or an absolute one, and the attempt continues. A write that resolves outside the worktree still ends the attempt.
acceptance_criteria: A command the hook refuses that contains a `cd` leaves the guard's working directory unchanged, so a later relative write is judged against the directory the shell is in.

A `cd` to an unreadable target in a command that ran marks the directory unknown, and the next relative write is refused as one command, with a reason naming the unknown directory and the fix, recorded as a denial; the attempt is not terminated.
A redirect or write whose destination resolves outside the worktree after any `cd` still ends the attempt with the same stop text.

issues.title: The seal reads the branch against its merge-base with the base ref, so a base that moved is never judged as the attempt's writes
issues.outcome: The change set an attempt is judged on is the branch against the merge-base of the branch and the ticket's base ref, never against the plan's original base commit, so when the base moved after the branch's last merge-up and the merge-up failed, the files the base changed are not read as the attempt's own writes, and the path rules judge only what the executor changed.
acceptance_criteria: A branch that merged the base at one commit, a base that then moved and changed `.focrux/config.json`, and a conflict round that edits one test file end with a change set naming that test file only.
`describeRange` is handed the merge-base of the branch and the base ref on every seal, including after an aborted merge-up.
A path the executor did write inside `.focrux/**` is still refused with the same stop text.

issues.title: Code comments cite only decisions the register holds and describe what the code does
issues.outcome: No comment or test name in the code cites a decision or ADR the register does not hold, or cites a kept one for a meaning its entry does not state, and none describes a mechanism the code does not have (D-111).
acceptance_criteria: A search of `apps`, `packages`, `tooling` and `scripts` for every decision and ADR id the register does not hold or the public tree does not carry, and every SCP id the backlog does not hold or the public backlog does not carry, finds none.
Every citation of a kept id matches that entry's meaning: a level that is never lowered, and the admission record, cite D-072 rather than D-010 or D-003 (`admit.ts`, `edit.ts`, `ticket.ts`).

Comments that describe a path jail, an open and a closed CLI build, a required number of corpus repeats, a security event raised for a denied host (`egress.ts`), or base-change detection reaching `plan_invalid` (`ticket.ts`) describe what the code does instead.

issues.title: The first release carries its product-regulation artefacts
issues.outcome: The first binary release ships with an SBOM, a vulnerability-handling policy, a disclosure contact and a declared support period (D-048).
acceptance_criteria: The release build produces an SBOM that is attached to the release.
`SECURITY.md` states the vulnerability-handling policy and the disclosure contact.
The release notes declare the support period.

issues.title: Release Focrux publicly as lianmatsuo/focrux
issues.outcome: Focrux is public as lianmatsuo/focrux, and from then on it is where Focrux is developed (D-076).
acceptance_criteria: lianmatsuo/focrux holds the tree, and its branches, pull requests and releases are where Focrux is developed.
Every corpus fixture is published in plantedbugs, and the public CI runs the regression suite against a pinned plantedbugs commit.
The first release carries a signed tag, a published SHA-256 and a build provenance attestation (D-046).

issues.title: A ticket reads `pr_open` only when a pull request exists
issues.outcome: An approved run without `--publish` leaves the ticket in a state that says the change is approved and unpublished, and publishing it later moves the ticket to `pr_open`.
acceptance_criteria: An approved run without `--publish` does not move the ticket to `pr_open`, and `focrux inspect` and `focrux list` say the change is approved and unpublished.
A later run with `--publish` moves the ticket to `pr_open`.

issues.title: A conflict round learns which tickets merged under its branch from branches named by ticket id
issues.outcome: The re-level finds the tickets that merged into the base since a branch's last merge-up, whose branches carry the ticket id rather than its key, so a conflict round is briefed with their approved contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Given a base whose history merged a loop branch named `fcx/<ticket id>/<slug>` or `ayo/<ticket id>/<slug>`, the re-level names that ticket among those merged under the branch.
The re-level and `naming.ts` derive a ticket's branch segment the same way, from one function.

issues.title: Read the reviews other tools leave on Focrux's pull requests
issues.outcome: Reviews other tools leave on a pull request Focrux opened are read as external data and their findings routed like the reviewer's own (D-088).
acceptance_criteria: `focrux sync` reads the review comments other accounts leave on the pull request, labelled `external` (D-035).
Each such finding is routed by the same matrix as Focrux's own findings, and its source is recorded.
Text in those reviews never occupies an instruction position.

issues.title: A P3 change is reviewed by a model of a different family
issues.outcome: At P3 the reviewer runs on a model family other than the executor's, and the review records which (D-037).
acceptance_criteria: A P3 review runs on a configured reviewer of a different family from the executor, or stops for a person when none is configured.
Such a review records `independence.model_family: different`.

issues.title: The workspace budget reclaims worktrees by total size
issues.outcome: When the worktrees on a machine exceed `local_workspace_bytes`, idle leases are reclaimed oldest first until the total fits, as well as stale ones (D-049).
acceptance_criteria: Provisioning over the budget reclaims idle leases, oldest first, before it refuses.
A lease that a live run holds is never reclaimed.

issues.title: A ticket's status is projected to its source issue
issues.outcome: A ticket admitted from a tracker issue writes its status to that issue one way, and nothing on the issue is read after admission (D-003).
acceptance_criteria: When the ticket's state changes, the source issue receives the new status.
No field on the source issue is read after admission.

issues.title: The co-founder runs their work through Focrux
issues.outcome: The co-founder has Focrux installed and takes their own work from admission to a merged pull request with it.
acceptance_criteria: The co-founder has taken at least one ticket from admission to merge with Focrux.

issues.title: Pair the phone with the desktop over the local network
issues.outcome: A phone pairs with the desktop over the local network and shows the surfaces the phone boards draw, from the desktop's records, with no hosted service between them (D-097, D-075).
acceptance_criteria: A phone pairs with the desktop on the same network, and either side can revoke the pairing.
The phone shows what the phone boards draw, read from the desktop, and nothing passes through a hosted service.

issues.title: Publish the trademark, hosted-service, patent and dependency policies
issues.outcome: The public repository says how the Focrux name may be used, what a hosted service built on Focrux may call itself, and how patents and third-party dependencies are handled.
acceptance_criteria: A trademark and hosted-service policy is published beside the licence.
A patent and dependency policy is published, and the dependency licences the release carries are checked against it.

issues.title: Run only the checks a change's packages affect
issues.outcome: A run can limit its pinned checks to the packages its change touches, so a small change in a large monorepo does not pay for the whole suite.
acceptance_criteria: The run configuration can select checks per package, and a run picks them from the change set's paths.
Without a selection the full pinned set runs.
A change that grows beyond its declared scope still blocks.

issues.title: Lower a bundle's replay tier as its inputs expire
issues.outcome: A run bundle's replay tier drops when an input it needs expires or a provider retires the model version, and `focrux inspect` lists the replay modes that remain (D-039).
acceptance_criteria: Expiring an input, or retiring a model version, lowers the tier of every bundle that needs it, and records why.
`focrux inspect` shows a bundle's current tier and the replay modes it still supports.
issues.notes: Builds D-039. Until then the tier is set when a bundle is written and never lowered.

issues.title: Show the desktop's degraded states for what they are
issues.outcome: The desktop tells a person which degraded state a run is in, so a silent runner, a provider failure and an unfinished review each read differently.
acceptance_criteria: A runner that has gone silent is shown apart from a provider failure.
A review that errored or did not finish shows as a closed gate, never as a pass.
The desktop shows a run's scope escapes, file by file.

issues.title: Attach rule authority to the rule family
issues.outcome: Demotion and authority attach to a rule's family, the first dotted segment of its id, and the verdict schema holds the families as a closed enum (D-052).
acceptance_criteria: `packages/review/src/suppression.ts` demotes by family, not by full rule id.
The verdict schema has a closed family enum; the full rule id stays free text and keys the finding.
The pull request carries a regression-suite run (D-010).
issues.notes: Builds D-052. Until then authority is demoted per full rule id.

issues.title: Record which command wrote each file
issues.outcome: Each command record names the files the command wrote, so a hand edit to a generated path is a recorded fact rather than caught only where the contract declares its generated sources (D-062).
acceptance_criteria: A command record lists the files the command wrote.
Review tells a generated file from a hand edit by that record.

issues.title: An escalated ticket reaches merged when its pull request merges
issues.outcome: When a ticket stopped at `changes_requested` because the loop escalated declined findings to a person, and the person then approves and the pull request merges, `sync` walks the record to `merged` with the merge on its delivery, so `focrux stops` counts the merge and `escapes` opens its window; a ticket at `changes_requested` because a review refused it and whose pull request was closed unmerged stays where it is.
acceptance_criteria: Tests fail first: a ticket at `changes_requested` with declines on its last round and an open pull request that `gh` then reports merged syncs to `merged`; the same state with the pull request closed unmerged stays `changes_requested`.
Once merged, the ticket is classified by `unattendedMergeStatus` like any other merged ticket.
The state table in docs/04 names the route.

revision_note: The backlog holds open work. Ids are stable and opaque; a new entry is written SCP-NEW-<label> and numbered when its pull request merges (D-110).
